method: ORDER OF JUDGEMENT (Lilly, Christian Astrology 1647, Book III), VERIFIED against page images of the Wellcome copy of the 1647 edition (archive.org b30338724; printed page = PDF leaf minus 34; running head 'An Introduction to Nativities' for Book III). (1) NATAL PROMISE first: significators of the topic scored by essential and accidental dignity, judged by plurality of testimonies (p.561 'determine according to the plurality of testimonies'; table p.115). (2) ANNUAL PROFECTION second (Chap. CLXVI-CLXXI, p.715-733); Lilly says profections of themselves without directions are of little value (p.719), so strength 2. Bonatti (Pars V p.817-818, 1550) reads profection and revolution together. (3) SOLAR RETURN third (p.734-741). (4) TRANSITS last (p.741, day scale). Firdaria (Bonatti Pars V p.813-814) is a parallel period-lord. Directions are out of scope. WHAT CHANGED IN VERIFICATION: all tables compared cell by cell (see tables and western-verification-report.md); rules marked 'confirmed' were seen on the page, 'corrected' were restated from the page. The 32 held-back rules were re-derived from the pages where the passage could be read; the first reading's original condition text was not available to the verifier, so each is stated in full here. Four items stay unverified and are NOT in this file: lilly.general.plurality (a method statement, not a rule), lilly.travel.success-danger (page not read), valens.profection.pair-verdict and table E (the pair table was not found in the Riley text read). COMPUTABLE VALUES: 'now', 'small-addition', and the new 'needs-return-chart' for rules that need the planetary positions at the solar return, which the engine does not compute in v1; those are verified but cannot be bound yet. DIFFERENCES FROM THE ENGINE: Lilly's terms are Ptolemy's, not the Egyptian bounds in dignities.ts; two triplicity rulers per element by day and night, water is Mars for both (p.102, p.105: 'according to Ptolomy and Naibod'); Lilly's profection moves the Ascendant 30 degrees a year with two lords in a year when it crosses a sign (days truncated, p.727); Lilly uses Regiomontanus houses while the engine has whole-sign only (labelled variant). SIGNS NOTE: Lilly's glyphs in the 1647 print are read from the page images; where the glyph set is ambiguous the condition says so. Quotations are at most 25 words in the original spelling with the long s written as s. SECOND CHECK (second reader): see secondCheck and the section at the end of western-verification-report.md. Riley page numbers are the folios printed at the FOOT of each page.

Lilly's alternative (Book III p.733-734): 'Lords of the Septenniall yeers, vulgarly called Lords of the Alfridary': day birth Sun the first seven years, Venus the next seven, Mercury the next seven, 'and so in order'; night birth Moon the first seven years, Saturn the next seven, then (glyph on p.734, read as Jupiter) the next seven; this is a seven-year scheme and is not bound. Profection arithmetic (Lilly p.715-718, 727): 30 degrees a year from solar return to solar return; a degree of profection is 12 days 4 hours 12 minutes (p.718), equal to 365.2422/30 = 12.174 days; Lilly drops the hours (23 deg 23 min = 284 days 16 hours, read as 284, p.727), so days are truncated, not rounded. rules.name: Planetary strength classes from Lilly's dignity scores
rules.condition: For each planet compute E (essential score, Table A, sect-aware triplicity) and A (accidental score, Table B). CLASS IS DEFINED ON E ALONE (derived, not Lilly's wording): STRONG if E >= +3; MODERATE if E is +1 or +2; WEAK if E < 0; E = 0 is unclassed (no signal). A is carried as a separate flag 'afflicted' if A <= -5, so a planet is never in two classes. The thresholds 3 and -5 are the implementer's operationalisation of Lilly's words; only the scores in the tables are his. A planet in its own term or face is not peregrine (p.103). 'Benevolent significator' (p.560) = Jupiter, Venus, or any planet standing in the dignities of a good planet.
rules.template: {planet} is {class} in this chart (essential {E}, accidental {A}{afflictedFlag}).
rules.sourceCitation: William Lilly, Christian Astrology (London, 1647), Book I Chap. XVIII p.101-104 and table p.115; Book III Chap. CXVI p.560
rules.sourceLocator: Book I p.101 (house = five), p.102 (exaltation four, triplicity three, terme two), p.103 (face one; own decanate or face is not peregrine), p.104 (table), p.115 (scores); Book III p.560 (benevolent significator)

rules.variants: Egyptian bounds (engine now) and Dorothean three-ruler triplicities give different E values. Lilly counts mutual reception by house as 5 and by exaltation as 4 (p.115).
rules.verificationNote: Scores (5, 4, 3, 2, 1; detriment -5, fall -4, peregrine -5; reception 5 and 4) seen on p.115 and in the text of p.101-103. Sect-aware triplicity seen on p.102 (the Sun by night does not rule the fiery triplicity, Jupiter does). The class thresholds are not in Lilly and stay labelled derived. E = 0 is left unclassed here because the original left it undefined.

rules.name: Wealth promise: significators of substance strong and angular
rules.condition: S_w = {domicile lord of the 2nd cusp sign; each planet in the 2nd (house from 5 degrees before the 2nd cusp to 5 degrees before the 3rd, or whole-sign variant); domicile lord of the sign holding the Part of Fortune; Jupiter}. (Lilly also lists the lord of an intercepted sign and 'the Lords' of the Part of Fortune; interception does not exist in whole signs, and the engine uses the domicile lord only.) Part of Fortune = Asc + Moon - Sun by day, Asc + Sun - Moon by night. Fires if MORE THAN HALF of S_w stand in angles (1, 4, 7, 10) and the same significators are essentially dignified (derived: more than half of S_w STRONG, class on E). Verdict: a very great estate, plenty of all things. The moderate case is its own rule (lilly.wealth.promise-moderate). Combinations not covered by the strong, moderate, weak, mixed rules emit NO signal.

rules.condition: Either (a) the Moon is combust (same sign as the Sun, within 8 deg 30', p.113) and her dispositor is an Infortune (Saturn or Mars); or (b) the sign-degree of the prenatal conjunction or opposition of the Sun and Moon (Lilly's glyphs here are conjunction and opposition, not the Part of Fortune) is oppressed by the Infortunes and they are cadent, the lord of that place being an Infortune and strong, or Jupiter cadent with a dispositor not potent. rules.name: Lord of the year from the profected Ascendant (Lilly by-degree; two lords when the sign changes)
rules.condition: Lilly gives 30 degrees to a solar year (p.715-716): the profected Ascendant at time t = natal Ascendant + 30 * (years elapsed since birth, fractional); a year runs from solar return to solar return (p.716). Lord of the year = domicile lord of the sign of the profected Ascendant (p.720, p.727). If the profected Ascendant crosses into the next sign during the year there are two lords: the first rules for the arc remaining to the sign boundary at 12 days 4 hours 12 minutes per degree (p.718; = 365.2422/30 per degree), counted in WHOLE DAYS with the hours dropped (Lilly's example: 23 deg 23 min = 284 days 16 hours, he reads 284, p.727), then the lord of the next sign rules until the next solar return. If the year begins at 0 degrees of a sign there is one lord. The whole-sign variant is the same fact as valens.profection.transmission-lord and runs there only.

rules.name: Aspects and orbs as Lilly gives them
rules.condition: Five aspects only (p.105): conjunction (0), sextile (60), square (90), trine (120), opposition (180). Sextile and trine friendly (trine more forcible), square imperfect enmity, opposition perfect hatred, conjunction good or bad as the planets are friends or enemies (p.106). Partile = same degree and minute; platick = within the sum of the two planets' moieties (p.106-107; his example Venus 4 + Saturn 5 = 9). Orbs, first column (p.107): Saturn 10, Jupiter 12, Mars 7 30', Sun 17, Venus 8, Mercury 7, Moon 12 30'; second column ('according to others', which Lilly says he also uses): Saturn 9, Jupiter 9, Mars 7, Sun 15, Venus 7, Mercury 7, Moon 12. Combustion within 8 deg 30' of the Sun in the same sign; under the beams to 17 degrees; cazimi within 17 minutes (p.113). Superior planets (Saturn, Jupiter, Mars) oriental from conjunction to opposition; Venus and Mercury oriental when fewer degrees of the sign the Sun is in, or in the sign before; Mercury never more than 28 and Venus never more than 48 degrees from the Sun, 'though some allow a few more' (p.114). Besieged between Saturn and Mars (p.114).

rules.name: Bonatti: which profection to read for which topic
rules.condition: Bonatti names the profection (a whole sign a year) whose sign is read: honours and annual dignities from the profection of the Sun; body and soul from the Moon; magistracies and offices from the Midheaven; gain and prosperity from the profected sign of the Part of Fortune and of the house of substance (2nd); brothers from the 3rd house; father from the 4th; children from the 5th; servants from the 6th; wives, partners and enemies from the 7th; the wives' substance from the house of their substance (8th); religious men from the 9th; kings from the 10th; friends from the 11th; hidden enemies from the 12th. The profected lord of the year is called alcocoden, which Bonatti glosses as 'participant in accidents' (his own gloss).

rules.name: Revolution: return Ascendant the same sign as the natal Ascendant
rules.condition: The solar-return Ascendant sign equals the natal Ascendant sign. Verdict: good: good health, actions succeeding, and increase of substance if the lord of the Ascendant is also well dignified (class STRONG or E >= +1, derived). If that lord is combust: much mischief according to the nature of the planet that is lord of the year; the Moon strong or in her dignities, chiefly by night, diminishes it.
rules.template: The return Ascendant is in the natal Ascendant sign: Lilly reads a good year{lordClause}.
rules.sourceCitation: William Lilly, Christian Astrology (London, 1647), Book III Chap. CLXXII
rules.sourceQuote: If the ascendant of the Revolution doe agree, or be the same with the ascendant of the Radix, it signifieth good

rules.name: Revolution: house of the lord of the second, the Part of Fortune or Jupiter
rules.condition: NEEDS THE RETURN CHART. Lilly's subject is the significators of the radix: the lord of the 2nd, the Part of Fortune and Jupiter of the birth chart, each taken at its place by longitude in the houses of the solar return. In whatever house of the revolution he finds them, he says the native shall have augmentation of patrimony or estate by the things that house signifies (Christian Astrology p.737, 'so observe in the rest'). The passage says through which house a gain comes and not whether the year is good: it attaches no strength, dignity or aspect requirement, so none was lost from the rule. The rule is therefore a pointer (direction activates) and gives one statement for each of the three significators. The page was re-read for this correction.
rules.template: In the return {significator}, one of the significators of money (the lord of the 2nd, the Part of Fortune and Jupiter of the birth chart), stands in the {h}th house: Lilly reads augmentation of estate through the things signified by that house.
rules.sourceCitation: William Lilly, Christian Astrology (London, 1647), Book III Chap. CLXXII
rules.sourceQuote: augmentation of Patrimony or Estate by things signified by that house
rules.variants: Regiomontanus versus whole-sign houses differ.
rules.verificationNote: Page re-read for this correction (Christian Astrology Book III p.736-737, Wellcome scan, page image read). The sentence is a reason and a consequence and attaches no condition of strength; the subject is the radical significators placed in the return houses, not the return chart's own lord of the 2nd. The direction is therefore activates, not favourable.

rules.name: Revolution: planets disposed contrary to the radix
rules.condition: NEEDS THE RETURN CHART. In a revolution in which the planets are all disposed contrary to the radix (all subterranean in the radix and all above the earth in the revolution, or all cadent in the radix and all in their own houses in the revolution), the year signifies ill, even if they are well disposed. Two extreme examples only.

rules.name: Revolution: a planet returns to its own radical place or to another's (money readings)
rules.condition: NEEDS THE RETURN CHART. In the revolution a planet is at the same degree (partile; Lilly gives no orb, derived) as a radical planet place. Money readings only: Saturn at its own radical place and well affected: dignity and store of substance, perhaps an inheritance; Saturn at Jupiter's place: fortunate in body and goods; Jupiter at its own place: a child and much wealth, health and esteem; Mercury at Saturn's place: profit by husbandry and wealth from old men; Mercury at Jupiter's place: acquires an office, gains by trade. Identification of the glyphs follows Lilly's fixed order of the list for each planet (Saturn, Jupiter, Mars, Sun, Venus, Mercury, Moon).

rules.name: Revolution: a planet returns to a place that afflicts (non-money readings)
rules.condition: NEEDS THE RETURN CHART. Same mechanism as lilly.revolution.returns-wealth. Readings kept: the Moon at the Sun's radical place: many hazards and dangers, sore eyes; the Moon at her own radical place ONLY WHEN she was weak at birth (class WEAK): much ill according to her signification at that time (her other branch, 'promises good if radically fortunate', is favourable and is not part of this rule). Mars at his own radical place is NOT coded: Lilly's sentence there is 'in danger by Fire, profit by Souldiers, or very much love and friendship', three alternatives of which the first version kept only the first. rules.name: Valens: which point to count the year from, by topic
rules.condition: Counting as in valens.profection.transmission-lord, Valens (IV.11) starts the count from: the Ascendant for length of life and body and mind; the Sun for rank, preeminence, the father, great personages; the Moon for dangers to health, diseases, bleeding, the mother; the MC for occupation, livelihood, work; the Lot of Fortune for good fortune and success in life; the Descendant for mortality, change, trouble (the first version softened the first word; the rule is a mapping of start to matter, and no output template uses the word); the IC for estates, possessions, secret matters, legacies; Venus for women, love affairs, associations; Mars for military or public matters; Saturn for bankruptcy, money or property, secret diseases, family inheritance; Jupiter for rank, friendship, alliances, possessions; Mercury for associations, servile matters, giving and receiving, written matters. This is a mapping of topic to start, with no numeric scale.

rules.name: Valens: a malefic holding the year, and a benefic or malefic transiting it
rules.condition: A malefic holds the year (is the chronocrator: the planet that receives the year per valens.profection.transmission-lord; implementer's identification). If another malefic transits the year (the profected sign), it intensifies the evil; if a benefic transits it, it brings relief and help (Riley p.108). NOT CODED: Valens's next sentence 'Assume the same is true for benefics' (it can mean a benefic year-lord with a benefic or a malefic transit; ambiguous), the retrograde clause ('delay expectations, actions, profits, and enterprises') which Valens states for all stars generally and not for the year-lord, and the phase clauses (rising, last visibility, stationary points), which need heliacal phase data.

unconfirmed.reason: Logical structure of the sentence is ambiguous. Lilly p.617: 'neither of the Lights in an angle or in a masculine Signe, or have not the benevolent Planets with them' gives 'abject people and of no quality'. Read as written, the two clauses are joined by 'or', and 'neither ... in an angle or in a masculine Signe' can mean not (angle or masculine) or (not angle) or (not masculine). The AND-reading is a narrowing that the text does not state. Left unbound until the director settles the reading; the cadent rule from the same passage is kept.
